subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should `chat.send` success require the WebChat user turn to be durably visible or abortably queued before returning `started`, or should delayed runtime-owned persistence remain the contract with separate visible recovery?
rationale: Current UI code mitigates stale history replacement, but changing the ACK boundary affects gateway latency, duplicate suppression, session rollover, hooks, and runtime-owned transcript ownership.

options.title: Require durable or queued before ACK
options.body: Make `chat.send` return success only after the user turn is durably visible or safely recoverable, with focused tests for normal, hook-gated, rollover, and active-run paths.

options.title: Keep delayed persistence with visible recovery
options.body: Leave runtime-owned persistence delayed but add explicit failed/retry notices so accepted sends cannot disappear silently.

options.title: Treat the UI mitigation as sufficient
options.body: Close the issue as addressed by optimistic-tail preservation and accept that durable transcript visibility is not part of the ACK contract.

recommendation.title: Require durable or queued before ACK
recommendation.body: Make `chat.send` return success only after the user turn is durably visible or safely recoverable, with focused tests for normal, hook-gated, rollover, and active-run paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans the Control UI mitigation and the user-turn recorder area most relevant to the remaining boundary decision.
